title: A limit order book
summary: The core data structure of every exchange: resting orders sorted by price with std::map, FIFO queues per price level, price-time priority matching, cancellations, and clear ownership through std::unique_ptr.

steps.title: Resting orders and best prices
hints: Bids sorted from highest price: `std::map<long, std::deque<Order*>, std::greater<long>>`. Asks: a plain `std::map` (lowest first).
Own the orders in `std::unordered_map<long, std::unique_ptr<Order>>`, and keep non-owning `Order*` in the price levels.

steps.title: Matching with price-time priority
hints: A buy at price P matches asks while `best_ask <= P`; a sell matches bids while `best_bid >= P`.
Always take the **front** of the best level's deque (oldest order) and trade at the **resting** order's price.
Remove fully filled orders from their level and from the owning map. Erase empty levels.

steps.title: Cancels and market orders
hints: `cancel`: find the order through the owning map, remove its pointer from the level's deque, erase the empty level, then erase the `unique_ptr` (which deletes the order).
A market order is a limit order that accepts any price and never rests: reuse the matching loop.
